dpc-vqa.name: DPC-VQA
dpc-vqa.takeaway: Keep the perceptual model. Learn the correction.
dpc-vqa.highlightContext: Among the compared few-shot methods, spanning UGC and AIGC.

steps.title: Perceive
steps.text: Extract quality cues, a base score and confidence from a frozen MLLM.

steps.title: Calibrate
steps.text: Combine visual and auxiliary video features to predict a bounded residual.

steps.title: Adapt
steps.text: Align the final score with human ratings using limited target-domain supervision.

dpc-vqa.headline: Calibrating a perceptual prior
dpc-vqa.intro: A pretrained MLLM provides a useful starting point for judging video quality, but its scores may not align with human ratings in a target dataset. DPC-VQA learns a residual correction while keeping the perceptual model frozen.
dpc-vqa.figureCaption: Figure 3 · Frozen quality perception and trainable residual calibration.
dpc-vqa.resultNote: SRCC, higher is better. The reference is the strongest compared few-shot method on each dataset—not a single model. DPC-VQA uses a 20% training pool with five-run averages; some dedicated fully supervised methods score higher.
dpc-vqa.method: The calibration branch combines visual and auxiliary video features with the model’s base score and confidence. It predicts a bounded correction rather than learning the quality score from scratch.
dpc-vqa.footnote: The perception backbone stays frozen during adaptation; only the calibration branch is optimized. The frozen model is still required at inference.

leaf.name: LEAF
leaf.takeaway: Learn quality from a teacher. Calibrate with human ratings.
leaf.highlightContext: 0.841 SRCC on AGIQA-3K with teacher-guided distillation and calibration.

steps.title: Teach
steps.text: A frozen multimodal teacher supplies quality scores and pairwise preferences.

steps.title: Distill
steps.text: Transfer these signals to a compact student, accounting for confidence.

steps.title: Calibrate
steps.text: Fine-tune the student with a small subset of human mean opinion scores.

leaf.headline: Separating perception from score calibration
leaf.intro: How much human supervision is needed to learn image quality—and how much is needed to calibrate its scoring scale? LEAF separates these roles through teacher-guided distillation followed by calibration with a small human-rated subset.
leaf.figureCaption: Figure 3 · Teacher-guided distillation followed by calibration fine-tuning.
leaf.resultTitle: Label budget and the contribution of distillation
leaf.resultNote: AGIQA-3K results. MOS availability is measured on the training split; label-budget results average five sampling runs. Zero human MOS still includes teacher supervision.
leaf.method: A frozen multimodal teacher provides quality judgments and pairwise preferences. A compact student learns from these signals before being fine-tuned to match human mean opinion scores.
leaf.footnote: The ablation holds the MOS budget at 10%. It separates the contribution of teacher-guided learning from the subsequent calibration stage.

vquala.taskCaption: Visual quality comparison tasks · examples from the challenge report.
vquala.name: VQualA 2025
vquala.takeaway: Compare visual quality through complementary model judgments.
vquala.highlightContext: We achieved 75.60% overall accuracy in the official challenge.

steps.title: Adapt
steps.text: Apply supervised fine-tuning and preference optimization to multimodal models.

steps.title: Compare
steps.text: Predict visual quality preferences across multiple input images.

steps.title: Vote
steps.text: Combine five models’ predictions into the final ensemble decision.

vquala.headline: Team Entry
vquala.intro: The Digital Ocean entry addresses visual quality comparison across multiple images. It combines supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization with a five-model voting ensemble.
vquala.figureCaption: Figure 4 · Digital Ocean team’s preprocessing, training and ensemble inference.
vquala.resultNote: Five valid final submissions. Digital Ocean placed second with 75.60% overall accuracy. Group-wise scores describe different test subsets and should not be read as evidence that more images make reasoning easier.
vquala.method: InternVL and Qwen models are adapted using the provided training data, with LoRA applied to the language components. Their predictions are combined by voting; the challenge report describes the team’s method in Section 5.2.
vquala.footnote: These results belong to the Digital Ocean entry. The linked publication is the multi-team challenge report.
